Inference (labeled): financialization can crowd out household buyers. Policy blame requires statutes and program designs, not only price charts.

CMHC insures over $500 billion in Canadian mortgages. This insurance allows lenders to extend credit with lower down payments — increasing the number of buyers who can enter the market. More buyers competing for limited supply drives prices up. Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) receive preferential tax treatment under Canadian tax law. REITs that distribute income to unitholders are not taxed at the entity level — meaning institutional ownership of residential property receives more favourable tax treatment than many small business structures. Municipal zoning restrictions limit density in many Canadian urban areas. Single-family zoning reserves large portions of major cities for low-density housing, limiting the construction of apartments and condominiums that could increase supply.
